about: si-expr: a JSON AST language (a superset of JSONLogic) for rules that must run the same in Node, Python, Rust and WebAssembly. Every interpreter implements exactly these operators; test/expr-vectors.json checks them. See lib/expr/README.md.
literals: An object is an operator only when it has exactly one key and that key is a known operator. Any other object is a literal (returned as is, not evaluated), except a single key starting with "si." that isn't known, which is an error.

var.about: Read a dotted path from the data; optional default

if.about: if/then/else-if chain; an even count without else gives null

and.about: First falsy value, else the last value

or.about: First truthy value, else the last value

in.about: Item in array, or substring in string

map.about: Evaluate the expression with each item as the data

filter.about: Keep items for which the expression is truthy

some.about: True when the expression is truthy for any item

all.about: True when the expression is truthy for every item (false for an empty array)

si.match.about: Ontology term match: lowercased matched words, or null. Case-insensitive; the match may not be preceded or (without *) followed by [a-z0-9]; a trailing * also takes the rest of the word [a-z0-9-]*

si.first_match.about: First matching term's matched words, or null; a single string counts as one term

si.matches.about: Every term's matched words, de-duplicated, in term order

si.count.about: Length of an array or string; 0 for null

si.unique.about: De-duplicate an array, keeping first occurrences

si.let.about: [{name: expr}, body]: bind names (evaluated in order, later ones see earlier ones), then evaluate body

si.obj.about: {key: expr}: build an object with each value evaluated

si.tpl.about: [template, data]: fill {{name}} (dotted paths allowed); arrays joined with ', '; null becomes empty
